m:catedral: Open Monday–Saturday 10:45am–7pm and Sunday 2:30–7pm; the ticket office closes at 6pm. Ticket €13 online, €14 at the desk (official website, page from 1 January 2026); reduced €7–8. The visit takes about 75 minutes and starts at the Giralda. On Sundays from 4:30 to 6pm there's free entry, but you must book online. Hours can change for services or events. On 4–8 December 2026 the International Congress of Brotherhoods restricts visits.
m:alcazar: From 1 April to 28 October open 9:30am–7pm, from 29 October to 31 March 9:30am–5pm, every day; closed on 1 and 6 January, Good Friday and 25 December. The basic ticket costs €15.50 (official Patronato fare from 2025; other guides still give €13.50–14.50, older prices: to be confirmed), plus €5.50 for the Cuarto Real Alto, the royal apartment, booked separately. Buy your ticket on the official website alcazarsevilla.org, the only authorised seller, with an entry time: in the busiest months it sells out. On Monday afternoons (4–5pm in winter) there's free entry with long queues and compulsory booking.
m:santacruz: Free to walk at any hour. In the middle of the day it's very crowded: early morning or late afternoon it has a much calmer atmosphere. Terraces with tables are often pricier than average.
m:plazaespana: The square is open every day from 8am to 10pm (Timeout, to be confirmed) and entry is free. You can rent boats on the canal, normally for €6–8 per boat for half an hour (price from guides, not read on the operator's website). In the afternoon there's shade only under the arcades.
m:torre: The museum is open Monday–Friday from 9:30am to 7pm and Saturday and Sunday from 10:30am to 7pm (Ministry of Defence listing); it closes on local and national holidays. Entry costs about €3 (reduced €1.50), free on Mondays according to some guides: prices not read on the official website, to be confirmed.
m:setas: The viewpoint is open from 9:30am to 11pm Sunday to Thursday and until 11:30pm on Friday and Saturday (Timeout, to be confirmed). The ticket costs about €15 (from guides, price not read on the official website: to be confirmed). In the basement is the Antiquarium, with the Roman and Moorish remains found during the excavations.
m:archivo: The visit is free. Hours: Tuesday–Saturday 9:30am–5pm, Sunday and holidays 10am–2pm; closed on Mondays; last entry 30 minutes before (from guides, to be confirmed on the Ministry of Culture website). Access may be limited if it fills up.
m:pilatos: Open every day from 9am to 6pm (Ticketlens, to be confirmed on fundacionmedinaceli.org). The ground floor costs €12 and the upper floor €6 more (prices from guides, to be confirmed).
m:triana: The market is normally open from 9am to 3pm with the stalls, and the bars inside stay open longer (hours from guides, to be confirmed). Calle Betis and the bridge are always open and free. Sunset over the river is the best time.
m:bellas: Open Tuesday 2:30–8:30pm, Wednesday–Saturday 9am–8:30pm, Sunday 9am–2:30pm; closed on Mondays (from sevillacitycentre.com, to be confirmed). Ticket €1.50; free for European Union citizens, Italians included, with ID.
m:sierpes: Free to walk. Shops are usually open 10am–2pm and 5–9pm; many close on Sundays and take a break in the early afternoon.
vd:rinconcillo: Seville's oldest tavern, open since 1670: a wooden bar, a beamed ceiling, and the bill chalked on the counter by the barman. Have a caña of beer with the day's tapas, like espinacas con garbanzos (spinach with chickpeas), albóndigas or solomillo al whisky.
vp:rinconcillo: A tapa usually costs €3–5; a light meal takes €15–20 per person (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:romero: A tavern that has been making the montadito de pringá, the hot roll with stewed meat, for decades, along with other Sevillian tapas. Eat standing at the bar or at a little table, with a caña or a glass of Condado wine.
vp:romero: A montadito costs €3–5; a simple meal is between €15 and €22 per person (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:morales: A bodega opened in 1850, with wine barrels, old earthenware jars and counter tapas: cheese, ham, tortilla and salmorejo, a cold tomato cream. Here you drink Montilla or Jerez wine.
vp:morales: A tapa or half-portion costs €3–6; eating well takes €14–20 per person (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:teresas: An 1870 bar in the Santa Cruz quarter, with hanging hams, azulejo walls and period photos: tapas of jamón, cola de toro (oxtail) and tortilla, with a glass of the house white.
vp:teresas: A tapa costs €3–6; a breakfast or snack €5–8 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:columnas: A bodega on the corner of Calle Mateos Gago, always full of Sevillians at tapas time, with tables in the street: house tapas and a plate of cold cuts; you order at the bar and they tally it in chalk.
vp:columnas: A tapa costs €3–5; a breakfast €4–6 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:campana: The historic 1885 pâtisserie at the start of Calle Sierpes: croissants, tostadas, yemas, sandwiches and sweets to take away or eat standing at the counter.
vp:campana: A coffee with a tostada costs about €4–6 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:mercado: The covered market on the site of the old San Jorge castle: stalls of fish, fruit and hams and bars serving fried-fish tapas, ceviche and tortillas. Go for breakfast or a quick lunch among the stalls.
vp:mercado: A tapa or a sandwich costs €3–6; a light lunch €10–16 (menu not seen). Hours and opening days from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:cuesta: A Triana tavern open since 1880, with a horseshoe bar and tables in the street: simple Andalusian cooking, with carrillada (braised pork cheek), salmorejo, pescado frito and wine from the barrel.
vp:cuesta: Tapas and half-portions €3–6; a meal is around €15–22 per person (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
cd:flamenco: A flamenco museum, with a small show in the patio.
cn:casamemoria: Flamenco show, Casa de la Memoria
cd:casamemoria: An hour of flamenco in a 19th-century patio, with few seats.
cx:casamemoria: Shows in the evening only, at fixed times: book.
cd:venerables: A Baroque palace in the Barrio de Santa Cruz, with a painted church.
cd:maestranza: Spain's most beautiful Baroque bullring, with a museum.
cd:duenas: The palace of the Dukes of Alba, with flower-filled patios.
cd:caridad: A Baroque church with paintings by Murillo and Valdés Leal.
cd:salvador: The city's second church, built on the site of the main mosque.
cd:guadalquivir: An hour on the river, between the Torre del Oro and Triana.
cd:islamagica: The exploration-themed amusement park, on the Isla de la Cartuja.
cx:islamagica: Only open in some seasons: check the calendar.
